newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan police chief sacked after student killings.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan police chief sacked after student killings.

text.p: Kenya's police commissioner was sacked on Thursday after two students were fatally shot by police during a demonstration at Nairobi's Kenyatta University,
"Police Commissioner Shedrach Kiruki has been retired," a brief statement from President Daniel arap Moi's office said.
Moi's office said Duncan Wachira, a highly respected crimebuster, had been appointed new police commissioner.
Meanwhile, 12 policemen were charged in the Nairobi court with the deaths at Kenyatta University. The men were not required to enter a plea on procedural grounds, court officials told Reuters.
The two Kenyatta University students died on Wednesday when police started shooting during a protest against the police killing of a student at Egerton University in Njoro on Tuesday.
Opposition leaders had demanded Kiruki's resignation over the three deaths and a group of opposition MPs went to Kiruki's office and gave him a letter calling for him to step down.
Earlier, senior Superintendent Peter Kimanthi at police headquarters in Nairobi said police firearms were taken for ballistic tests to identify who fired the fatal shots.
Kimanthi said a public inquest would be held into the death of the Egerton student whom he said was shot when students tried to snatch guns from police.

A government statement issued on Wednesday said police had been called in to Kenyatta University after reports students were on the rampage, stoning cars, building barricades and lighting fires on a main road outside campus.
"Police shot in the air several times as a result of which the students ran back to the campus from where they engaged the police in a running battle," the government statement said.

"The police continued firing in the air as the skirmishes continued. The government is deeply saddened by the police action which led to the death of two students and serious injuries to three others," the statement added.

But George Eshiwani, Kenyatta University's vice-chancellor, said the protests were peaceful and he had gave firm instructions police should not enter the campus on Wednesday because students were mourning their dead colleague.
"The students were not violent in any way. Why? Why had this to happen? You only needed to fire teargas and nothing more," he was quoted as telling a police officer after the shooting.

The Egerton University students were protesting over a refund of 504 shillings ($9.89) they said each of them was owed by the administration. The students also wanted the release of one of their leaders remanded by a court for inciting violence.
